support_spans: multiple bilateral, symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions in the periventricular and periaqueductal regions, dorsomedial thalami, medial temporal lobes, caudate nuclei, and brainstem, with diffusion restriction and low ADC values
Spinal MRI demonstrated diffuse T2 hyperintensities throughout the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar cord
progressive neurological deficits
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with ADEM, a rare autoimmune disease characterized by widespread demyelination of the central nervous system.

selector.rationale: The presence of multiple bilateral, symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions in the periventricular and periaqueductal regions, dorsomedial thalami, medial temporal lobes, caudate nuclei, and brainstem, with diffusion restriction and low ADC values, along with progressive neurological deficits and spinal cord involvement, supports ADEM as the most likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Multiple Sclerosis (MS)
rejected.why: While MS could explain some of the findings, the acute onset and progression of symptoms, along with the presence of diffusion restriction and low ADC values, are more suggestive of ADEM.

rejected.label: Acute Transverse Myelitis
rejected.why: The presence of widespread brain lesions in addition to spinal cord involvement makes ADEM a more comprehensive diagnosis.

rejected.label: Subacute Combined Degeneration (SCD) due to Vitamin B12 Deficiency
rejected.why: The lack of specific findings suggestive of vitamin B12 deficiency, such as macrocytic anemia or elevated homocysteine levels, makes this diagnosis less likely.
